requirements.rationale: Today it is 290 to 667px; the chosen design measured 154px.
requirements.statement: On the spec page in a 1920x1080 window with the header expanded, the first line of the document body starts at most 200px below the top of the spec header, whatever messages, warnings and facts are showing.

requirements.rationale: Today it is 459 to 874px; the chosen design measured 248 to 276px with the panel's four navigation rows kept.
requirements.statement: In the conversation's side panel in a 1920x1080 window, with the conversation column at its default 480px and the header expanded, the first line of the body starts at most 320px below the top of the spec header, the tabs and section navigation included, whatever messages are showing.

requirements.rationale: Each message adding its own height is what made the body shrink with every warning. The operator chose the count (B) over a line (A) and a side column (C).
requirements.statement: However many messages and warnings a document has, they add no height above the body: the header shows their count, in the tone of the most urgent, and the count opens all of them, each on one line with its full text and its action reachable from there.

Once the body is scrolled away from its top, the header condenses to a single line of at most 48px, in the page and in the panel, still showing the title, the phase, the message count, the primary action and the More menu; it expands again when the body returns to its top or the line is clicked.

Every action, navigation, message, fact and detail panel the header and the banner offer today stays available from the header, the message list or the body; each action reachable today without opening a menu is still reachable without opening one, except a message's own action and the journey-step and size control, which are one click away.

requirements.rationale: Open by default it took most of the list's column on the operator's project (14 changes, 72 defects).
requirements.statement: The spec list's defects report starts folded to one line showing the number of defects, and opens only when the operator opens it.

In roadmap order, in every list of specs, every change document that names a roadmap slice is listed under that roadmap, in the roadmap's slice order, whether or not the spec index records a parent for it.

requirements.rationale: Today approved and done are the same green dot. The operator chose set 2 (paperwork) on the mock, and asked that it apply wherever specs are listed.
requirements.statement: Wherever a spec's state is marked in a list of specs (the Spec tab's column, the side panel's Open a spec screen including its cards, its Specs switcher, and the search dialog), each state has its own icon (writing, ready, approved, building, done, capability, archived), done is a solid green disc with a check, and no two states share an icon.

requirements.rationale: The operator opens the list to find what is waiting on them; no other order answers that.
requirements.statement: Every list of specs offers a 'What needs you' order that groups documents as Waiting on you, In progress, Approved not started, Finished and Capabilities, and shows beside each waiting document why: ready to approve, amendments to review, ready to build, or ready to fold.

For every document it lists, the Hub returns the roadmap and slice the document names, if any, and which of these hold: being written with nothing blocking approval, amendments unreviewed or proposed, approved with open tasks and no build, done and not folded.
The shipped header and lists match the mock the operator approved, in the page and in the panel, in each state the mock shows.

A document's header shows its phase and the actions open to it as buttons: Check while it is being written (never changing its phase), Approve when it is ready, Build or 'Approve and build' once it may be built, with the one the document is waiting for visually primary.
Pressing Check shows what blocks approval and what only warns, beside the parts of the document they concern, without leaving the page or freezing the document.

requirements.rationale: Filtering and ordering inside a document, and showing each requirement's evidence and each task's build state beside it, are not possible in a sandboxed frame of pre-rendered HTML. The operator approved replacing the frame (2026-10-26).
requirements.statement: The document's sections, requirements, acceptance criteria and tasks are rendered by the app from the document's structure, so the page can filter, order, highlight and link them.

The document list can be filtered by kind, phase, text and 'has a build running', ordered by last change, phase, title or roadmap order, and grouped under its roadmap, and the choice persists per project.
Within a document, requirements can be filtered by evidence state and by task, and tasks by status and agent; tasks can be ordered by status or by build order (dependencies).

An outline of the open document jumps to any section, requirement or task; a slice links to its roadmap and to the previous and next slice; back and forward return to the previous position; every position has a link that reopens it.

Each build of the document shows, live: its driver, level and people; tasks by status; wall time split into building, waiting for review, checks and waiting to be handed out; runs; and cost split between building, reviewing and leading.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26, approving the mock: 'don't forget that should be on the side panel as well'.
requirements.statement: The conversation's spec side panel shows the same document, actions, navigation and build progress as the Spec tab, in a layout that fits the panel's width.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26: 'a better navigation of the spec side panel, better filtering and ordering' (approved: 'that's amazing, keep this').
requirements.statement: The side panel switches to any other document from a switcher above its tabs; jumps to any section, and to any requirement or task from a strip that shows each one's state, with previous and next and its position; and filters and orders from one tray whose active choices stay visible as chips that remove themselves one at a time or all at once.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26: 'when we open the side panel and open specs we open a navigation to choose the spec to open, I want that improved as well' (approved: 'It works. Perfect'). Attaching stays the composer's control (SpecIndexTab design D9).
requirements.statement: Choosing a spec to open, from the panel's Specs tab, the Ctrl/Cmd+K picker or the panel's switcher, is one picker: a search field from which Enter opens the first match it names; with nothing typed, shortcuts to the conversation's attached document, to documents with a build running (with their progress) and to the last three opened; then every document with the Spec tab's filters, order and roadmap grouping. Opening never attaches a document to the conversation.

The page uses only the app's tokens and primitives, works in dark and light, animates state changes (opening, checking, a build's progress) with the motion tokens, and stops animating under reduced motion.

requirements.rationale: Operator practice since 2026-10-20: mocks are real components, so applying the approved mock is wiring, not redrawing.
requirements.statement: A mock of the Spec tab and the side panel, built from the real components fed recorded fixtures under hub/ui/mock, is approved by the operator before the page is wired to the Hub.
